results.reason: Issue 4 identifies automatic five-year renewals under SA §2.2 with notice due 240–270 days before expiry. It calculates the window as roughly June 3–4 to July 3–4, 2026, which is a 30-day window. It explains that missing it commits Harrowgate through about February 2032.

Issue 5 identifies the all-glass-and-PET, any-beverage, worldwide exclusivity in SA §3.1. It compares this with the term sheet's amber beer bottles at U.S./Canada facilities and notes that SA §15.1 supersedes the term sheet, so the broader text binds.

Issue 1 notes receipt on August 3, 2026 per Recital C and an objection deadline of September 2, 2026 under §5.4. It concludes the increase is deemed accepted and binding, before the September 21 amendment.

Issue 2 explains that Am. §2.1 replaces §11.2, removes the recall carve-out, and limits the indemnity carve-out to §9.1(c) IP claims. It states that recall and product-liability indemnities are now subject to the six-month-fees cap.

Issue 3 identifies new §14.4 permitting assignment without consent to Affiliates and successors, and notes Harrowgate remains bound by §14.3. However, it never explains that nothing prevents assignment to a competitor.
The response never states that under SA §15.2 written amendments take precedence over the Supply Agreement. It mentions §15.2 only regarding the QA and Purchase Orders.
Issue 8 and Issue 2 state that the §11.1 cap equals fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.
The response is a memo to the Supervising Partner. It lists issues item by item, each with a 'Where' section citing the document and section, and a recommended fix.
It proposes specific language for several fixes, including a restored §11.2, a narrowed §3.1, and a conditional assignment clause in §14.4.
The response concludes the objection window closed on September 2 and the increase appears binding. It does not treat the window as open.
The response states the term sheet is superseded and Harrowgate cannot rely on TS §2 as a contractual term.
